terms.definition:
"Judiciary" means the courts of the state, including any municipal
or district court, whether or not of record.

"State legislature" means the legislature of the state of New York,
including any committee, subcommittee, joint committee, select
committee, or commission thereof.

"Agency" means any state or municipal department, board, bureau,
division, commission, committee, public authority, public corporation,
council, office or other governmental entity performing a governmental
or proprietary function for the state or any one or more municipalities
thereof, except the judiciary or the state legislature.

"Record" means any information kept, held, filed, produced or
reproduced by, with or for an agency or the state legislature, in any
physical form whatsoever including, but not limited to, reports,
statements, examinations, memoranda, opinions, folders, files, books,
manuals, pamphlets, forms, papers, designs, drawings, maps, photos,
letters, microfilms, computer tapes or discs, rules, regulations or
codes.

"Critical infrastructure" means systems, assets, places or things,
whether physical or virtual, so vital to the state that the disruption,
incapacitation or destruction of such systems, assets, places or things
could jeopardize the health, safety, welfare or security of the state,
its residents or its economy.

"Law enforcement disciplinary records" means any record created in
furtherance of a law enforcement disciplinary proceeding, including, but
not limited to:

"Law enforcement disciplinary proceeding" means the commencement of
any investigation and any subsequent hearing or disciplinary action
conducted by a law enforcement agency.

"Law enforcement agency" means a police agency or department of the
state or any political subdivision thereof, including authorities or
agencies maintaining police forces of individuals defined as police
officers in section 1.20 of the criminal procedure law, a sheriff's
department, the department of corrections and community supervision, a
local department of correction, a local probation department, a fire
department, or force of individuals employed as firefighters or
firefighter/paramedics.

"Technical infraction" means a minor rule violation by a person
employed by a law enforcement agency as defined in this section as a
police officer, peace officer, or firefighter or firefighter/paramedic,
solely related to the enforcement of administrative departmental rules
that (a) do not involve interactions with members of the public, (b) are
not of public concern, and (c) are not otherwise connected to such
person's investigative, enforcement, training, supervision, or reporting
responsibilities.

"Retiree" means a former officer or employee of an agency, the
state legislature, or the judiciary who was a member of a public
retirement system of the state, as such term is defined in subdivision
twenty-three of section five hundred one of the retirement and social
security law and is receiving, or entitled to receive, a benefit from
such public retirement system.

"Beneficiary" means a person designated by a member or retiree of
a public retirement system of the state to receive retirement or death
benefits following the death of the member or retiree.

terms.definition: "Public body" means all legislative, executive, administrative, or advisory bodies of the State, state universities and colleges, counties, townships, cities, villages, incorporated towns, school districts and all other municipal corporations, boards, bureaus, committees, or commissions of this State, any subsidiary bodies of any of the foregoing including but not limited to committees and subcommittees thereof, and a School Finance Authority created under Article 1E of the School Code.

"Public body" does not include a child death review team or the Illinois Child Death Review Teams Executive Council established under the Child Death Review Team Act, or a regional youth advisory board or the Statewide Youth Advisory Board established under the Department of Children and Family Services Statewide Youth Advisory Board Act.
"Person" means any individual, corporation, partnership, firm, organization or association, acting individually or as a group.

"Public records" means all records, reports, forms, writings, letters, memoranda, books, papers, maps, photographs, microfilms, cards, tapes, recordings, electronic data processing records, electronic communications, recorded information and all other documentary materials pertaining to the transaction of public business, regardless of physical form or characteristics, having been prepared by or for, or having been or being used by, received by, in the possession of, or under the control of any public body.

"Private information" means unique identifiers, including a person's social security number, driver's license number, employee identification number, biometric identifiers, personal financial information, passwords or other access codes, medical records, home or personal telephone numbers, and personal email addresses.
Private information also includes home address and personal license plates, except as otherwise provided by law or when compiled without possibility of attribution to any person.

For a public body that is a HIPAA-covered entity, "private information" includes electronic medical records and all information, including demographic information, contained within or extracted from an electronic medical records system operated or maintained by the public body in compliance with State and federal medical privacy laws and regulations, including, but not limited to, the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act and its regulations, 45 CFR Parts 160 and 164.
terms.note: extension of the (c-5) definition for HIPAA-covered public bodies

terms.definition: As used in this subsection, "HIPAA-covered entity" has the meaning given to the term "covered entity" in 45 CFR 160.103.

"Commercial purpose" means the use of any part of a public record or records, or information derived from public records, in any form for sale, resale, or solicitation or advertisement for sales or services.

For purposes of this definition, requests made by news media and non-profit, scientific, or academic organizations shall not be considered to be made for a "commercial purpose" when the principal purpose of the request is (i) to access and disseminate information concerning news and current or passing events, (ii) for articles of opinion or features of interest to the public, or (iii) for the purpose of academic, scientific, or public research or education.

"Copying" means the reproduction of any public record by means of any photographic, electronic, mechanical or other process, device or means now known or hereafter developed and available to the public body.

"Head of the public body" means the president, mayor, chairman, presiding officer, director, superintendent, manager, supervisor or individual otherwise holding primary executive and administrative authority for the public body, or such person's duly authorized designee.

"News media" means a newspaper or other periodical issued at regular intervals whether in print or electronic format, a news service whether in print or electronic format, a radio station, a television station, a television network, a community antenna television service, or a person or corporation engaged in making news reels or other motion picture news for public showing.

"Recurrent requester", as used in Section 3.2 of this Act, means a person that, in the 12 months immediately preceding the request, has submitted to the same public body (i) a minimum of 50 requests for records, (ii) a minimum of 15 requests for records within a 30-day period, or (iii) a minimum of 7 requests for records within a 7-day period.

For purposes of this definition, requests made by news media and non-profit, scientific, or academic organizations shall not be considered in calculating the number of requests made in the time periods in this definition when the principal purpose of the requests is (i) to access and disseminate information concerning news and current or passing events, (ii) for articles of opinion or features of interest to the public, or (iii) for the purpose of academic, scientific, or public research or education.

For the purposes of this subsection (g), "request" means a written document (or oral request, if the public body chooses to honor oral requests) that is submitted to a public body via personal delivery, mail, telefax, electronic mail, or other means available to the public body and that identifies the particular public record the requester seeks.

"Voluminous request" means a request that: (i) includes more than 5 individual requests for more than 5 different categories of records or a combination of individual requests that total requests for more than 5 different categories of records in a period of 20 business days; or (ii) requires the compilation of more than 500 letter or legal-sized pages of public records unless a single requested record exceeds 500 pages.

"Voluminous request" does not include a request made by news media and non-profit, scientific, or academic organizations if the principal purpose of the request is: (1) to access and disseminate information concerning news and current or passing events; (2) for articles of opinion or features of interest to the public; or (3) for the purpose of academic, scientific, or public research or education.
"Single requested record" may include, but is not limited to, one report, form, e-mail, letter, memorandum, book, map, microfilm, tape, or recording.

For the purposes of this subsection (h), "request" means a written document, or oral request, if the public body chooses to honor oral requests, that is submitted to a public body via personal delivery, mail, telefax, electronic mail, or other means available to the public body and that identifies the particular public record or records the requester seeks.
"Severance agreement" means a mutual agreement between any public body and its employee for the employee's resignation in exchange for payment by the public body.

notes:
Gold standard (batch B: states ca, ny, il; 25 sections incl. the user's example Cal. BPC § 480) for statute cross-reference resolution and defined terms. Labeled by careful reading of I.text_of(state, id) from the lexflow index on 2026-10-10; a builder only located the exact spans/offsets and verified every citation. Totals: 319 references (276 resolvable in the index, 39 self-references), 154 term entries. References by kind: {'list_item': 94, 'section': 73, 'internal_relative': 66, 'pinpoint': 23, 'generic': 21, 'container': 21, 'other_code': 9, 'range': 4, 'federal': 3, 'regulation': 2, 'named_act': 2, 'court_rule': 1}. By role: {'scope': 147, 'exception': 37, 'procedure': 26, 'prerequisite_process': 23, 'condition': 23, 'other': 18, 'authority': 14, 'penalty': 13, 'override': 9, 'definition': 9}. Terms by kind: {'role/actor': 72, 'document': 43, 'thing': 16, 'other': 13, 'status': 6, 'process': 4}; by definition_type: {'used': 110, 'explicit': 24, 'functional': 6, 'by_reference': 6, 'limiting': 5, 'inclusive': 3}.

OFFSETS AND SPANS. start/end are Python str offsets into I.text_of(state, id); span == text[start:end] exactly (NY texts keep their hard line breaks, so some spans contain newlines). References are listed in text order and never overlap. list_span is the exact text of the whole coordinated list an item belongs to.

GRANULARITY. One entry per target phrase. Inline coordinated lists ('Section 1203.4, 1203.4a, ... or 1203.425 of the Penal Code', 'subdivision (a) or (b)', 'Sections 11505 and 11506') are split into one entry per item (the first item's span includes 'Section(s)'; later items are the bare number or pinpoint) with list_span set. A list that repeats its governing word ('pursuant to X or pursuant to Y') is two separate references. Vertically enumerated paragraphs (BPC 480(a)(1)(B)(i)-(v), VEH 42010(b)(1)-(15)) are separate references, not list items. A range ('Sections 11122 to 11127', 'Sections 37-21 through 37-30', 'subdivisions (a) through (p)') is one entry. Pinpoint phrases are one entry ('subparagraph (B) of paragraph (5) of subdivision (h) of Section 1170').

KIND. One kind per reference, by precedence: federal > constitution > court_rule > regulation > named_act > range > container > list_item > internal_relative > other_code > pinpoint > section, plus the extension kind 'generic' for references to unspecified other law ('any other law', 'any other provision of law', 'except as otherwise provided by law', 'Except as otherwise provided', 'statutory fees', 'otherwise fixed by statute', 'the governing statute of each of the other organizations'). So other_code is used only for a single section or pinpoint in another code or act of the same state ('Section 1192.7 of the Penal Code'); lists, ranges and containers into another code keep their structural kind, and target_code / target_code_name say which code. list_item applies to section- or pinpoint-shaped items of an inline list; a container inside a list stays 'container' (with list_span). internal_relative covers 'this chapter/article/Act/code/section/subdivision/subsection/definition' and 'any other provision of this code'. 'shape' gives the item's structural shape regardless of kind: section | pinpoint | range | container | unit | act | generic | regulation | court_rule.

TARGET_CODE / TARGET_SECTIONS. target_code is the qualifier as the text names it ('Penal Code', 'Vehicle Code', 'this article', 'this chapter', 'this Act', 'Limited Liability Company Law', 'criminal procedure law'); when the text names none it is the implied 'this code' (CA), 'this chapter' (NY consolidated law), 'this Act' (IL), or 'this section' for a pinpoint within the same section. target_code_name is the index's citation prefix ('Cal. PEN', 'N.Y. LLC Law', '805 ILCS 180'). target_sections are exact index citations; each one was confirmed with I.lookup(state, x) returning a row whose citation equals it (no citation had more than one row). Ranges list every section of the range the index holds (805 ILCS 180 numbers in steps of 5, so 37-21..37-30 is 37-21, 37-25, 37-30). Containers that say '(commencing with Section N)' list [N] with anchor=true, and target_unit is the index path prefix of the unit (e.g. 'California Code / Code bpc / Division 3 / Chapter 6'). Named acts and 'Article 1E of the School Code' list the act/article's short-title section as anchor plus target_unit ('Illinois Code / Chapter 20 / Act 515'; '105 ILCS 5/1E-*' is a citation pattern because IL paths have no article level). 'this chapter/article/Act/code' have target_sections null and target_unit set (resolvable when the unit exists). 'this section' and subsection-level self-references ('this subsection (g)', 'this definition', 'this subdivision') have target_sections [own citation], self=true, and a pinpoint when below section level; scorers that only want outward references should drop self=true. Same-section pinpoints ('subdivision (b)', 'paragraph (1)') have target_sections [own citation] and self=false. The anaphor 'those chapters' (BPC 480(f)(1)) lists all seven antecedent chapter anchors with anaphoric=true. Repealed or former sections (PEN 4852.01 'former Section 288a'; the PEN 1465.9 cost sections read 'as those sections read on June 30, 2021 / December 31, 2021', carried in as_of) have target_sections null and resolvable_in_index=false. acceptable_extra lists other defensible targets (VEH 42010 'Section 97 and following of the Streets and Highways Code': 97 is the Double Fine Zone section; 97.01 and 97.1 follow it). implied_pinpoint is a pinpoint the text does not state (PBO 86 cites CPL § 1.20 for 'police officers', which is subdivision 34). external gives a normalized citation for law outside the index (HIPAA, 45 C.F.R., Rules of Court, board regulations, house rules).

ROLE CONVENTIONS. definition: 'as defined in', 'has the meaning', 'as such term is defined in', 'set forth in' for the events/acts that make up a defined notion. exception: 'except as provided in', 'does not apply to', 'other than pursuant to', 'unless otherwise provided in', 'does not include ... established under', and 'subject to X' (X prevails over this rule). override: 'notwithstanding'. condition: the rule applies only if something in the target holds ('applies only when ... placed pursuant to', 'exempt under Section 7', 'fails to act within the time periods provided in Section 3', being subject to supervision under PEN 3451 / 1170(h)(5)(B), 'not inconsistent with law'). prerequisite_process: a status produced by another procedure ('dismissed pursuant to Section 1203.4', 'obtained a certificate of rehabilitation under Chapter 3.5', 'has made a showing of rehabilitation pursuant to Section 482', 'designated ... pursuant to Section 97 and following', 'formed under this chapter', 'continuation ... under section 701'). authority: a body acts under powers given there ('denial of a license by the board under Section 480', 'regulations adopted by the board', 'the agency designated pursuant to', protective orders 'issued by the court pursuant to', 'the powers granted by this chapter', 'requests permitted by Section 11505', 'the person winding up ... under Section 35-4'). procedure: 'in accordance with', 'as provided in Section 11509', 'for filing under', 'right to judicial review under Section 11'. penalty: fines, assessments and surcharges and their schedules. scope: lists what the rule covers (offenses 'specified in Section 290', the licensure chapters, the fee items of NY LLC § 1101, the costs made unenforceable by PEN 1465.9, 'As used in this article'). other: none of these (quoted form titles, a fee amount set elsewhere, copies of sections to be served).

EXCLUDED (not references): editorial source notes '(Source: P.A. ...)', '(from Ch. 116, par. 202)' and the '(5 ILCS 140/2)' header; private instruments (operating agreement, articles of organization, plan of merger, 'any contractual rights'); implicit references without citation text (GOV 11504 'served in the same manner as an accusation' (Section 11505); GOV 11512 review 'in the same manner ... as the proposed decision' (Section 11517); BPC 480 'substantially related' (Section 481); 5 ILCS 140/9 'Public Access Counselor'; 140/6(d) 'judicial review' (Section 11); 805 ILCS 180/5-1 'licensed physician'); 'conformed to and obeyed the laws of the land' (conduct, not a citation); 'a comparable dismissal or expungement' and 'clemency or a pardon by a state or federal executive' (outcomes, not citations).

TERMS. definition_type: explicit ('X means'), inclusive ('includes', 'may include', 'also includes'), limiting ('does not include', 'shall not apply'), by_reference ('has the meaning given', 'as defined in'; defined_in is the section that holds the meaning), functional (the section says what the thing is or does without a 'means' clause: 'organizer' NY LLC § 203(a), 'statement of issues' GOV § 11504, 'certificate of amendment' NY LLC § 211(a), the three revocation restitution fines of PEN § 1202.45), used (a term of art used here whose definition is in a governing definitions section; definition null). For defined-here entries defined_in is the section itself and defined_in_pinpoint the subdivision. Every defined_in / also_defined_in was verified with I.lookup. scope is the unit the governing definition covers ('this article', 'this Act', 'this division', 'Part 2 (commencing with Section 681)', 'this subsection (g)', 'Section 3.2 of this Act'). A term appears more than once when the section has more than one definitional sentence for it (5 ILCS 140/2 'Public body', 'Private information', 'Commercial purpose', 'Recurrent requester', 'Voluminous request'; 'request' is defined separately for subsections (g) and (h)). Used terms are limited to formally defined terms (PEN §§ 17, 691, 1203(a), 1170(h)(5)(B), 3451; BPC §§ 7.5, 22, 23.7, 23.8, 477, 478; GOV §§ 11500, 11503; VEH Division 1; NY LLC Law § 102; PBO § 86; 805 ILCS 180/1-5 and 37-5; 5 ILCS 140/2); undefined phrases such as 'certificate of rehabilitation', 'restitution fine', 'applicant' and 'plan of merger' are not listed. mentions are the surface forms found in the section. kind: role/actor | document | status | process | thing | other (offense classes such as felony are 'other').

WIKIDATA / LEXIPEDIA (read-only lookups, at most 1 request per second). wikidata_candidate is a concept-level QID, not a statute-specific definition: limited liability company Q149789 (US LLC), articles of organization Q16821865, operating agreement Q7096691, registered agent Q7309406, probation Q13961, felony Q178844, misdemeanor Q694324, administrative law judge Q4683585, public records Q7257959, news media Q1193236. The user's example Lexipedia Item:Q168 is Fla. Stat. § 607.0201 'Incorporators.', which is outside this batch. Its LLC counterpart here is 'organizer': a functional definition at N.Y. LLC Law § 203(a) (§ 102 has no entry) and the explicit 1-5 definition ('one of the signers of the original articles of organization') used in 805 ILCS 180/5-1 and 5-45. Wikidata has no matching legal-role item (the only 'incorporator' hit, Q140403634, is a PropBank semantic role), so incorporator/organizer would need its own Lexipedia concept item linking these sections. Nothing was written to Lexipedia or Wikidata.

OBSERVATIONS. N.Y. LLC Law § 211(d) cites 'subdivision (b) of this section' for the general power of amendment, which is stated in (a); it is labeled as written. The index does not hold the PEN cost sections repealed in 2021 that 1465.9 lists, or former PEN § 288a. 5 ILCS 140/6(d) writes 'subsections (6)(a) and (b) of this Act', meaning Section 6(a) and (b), i.e. this section.
